results.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
results.proof_sketch: Let T be r absorbing terminals and let N be the number of nonterminals. For t∈T, let h_t(v) be the probability that the uniform random walk is absorbed at t, and put g_t(v)=h_t(v)−h_t(s_0(v)). Harmonicity gives h_t(v)−h_t(s_1(v))=−g_t(v). For switching flows x,y with the same supply φ, write d_x(v)=x(v,s_0(v))−x(v,s_1(v)). Regrouping the weighted sum Σ_(u,v)(y−x)(u,v)(h_t(u)−h_t(v)) first by vertices and then by outgoing pairs proves x^−(t)−y^−(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v). The sum is over directed edges, so antiparallel arcs remain distinct and no shared antisymmetric residual-flow variable or residual-capacity identification is assumed. Hence every terminal coordinate differs by at most Σ_v|g_t(v)|≤N/2. Total terminal inflow is fixed at Σ_vφ(v); consequently, if terminal inflows are integral, at most (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(r−1) distinct terminal-inflow vectors are possible for fixed φ. This is polynomial for fixed r. Moreover, for φ≡1 every prescribed d∈[0,1]^N is realizable: solve t_v=1+Σ_{u:s_0(u)=v}(t_u+d_u)/2+Σ_{u:s_1(u)=v}(t_u−d_u)/2. Iteration from t≡1 stays at least 1 and converges because the nonterminal transition matrix is transient. The resulting edge flows are nonnegative. Thus, for two terminals the maximum possible difference is exactly Σ_v|g(v)|, obtained by choosing d_y−d_x=sign(g).

results.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
results.proof_sketch: Let m_i and M_i be the minimum and maximum zero-player hitting probabilities on L_i, and W_i=M_i−m_i. A walk starting at any level at least i must hit L_{i−1} before reaching a sink. The strong Markov property therefore expresses its hitting probability as a convex combination of the values on L_{i−1}. Hence m_{i−1}≤m_i≤M_i≤M_{i−1}. Both successors of v∈L_i have level at least i−1, so |g(v)|=|h(s_0(v))−h(s_1(v))|/2≤W_{i−1}/2. For r vertices per positive level, Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_i W_{i−1}. This precisely reduces harmonic-flow stability to controlling the cumulative nested level ranges, but does not give a constant bound.

results.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
results.proof_sketch: For k≥2 set L_i={a_i,b_i,c_i}, with a_0=0 and b_0=1. For i<k use edges a_i→(a_{i−1},a_{i+1}), b_i→(b_{i−1},b_{i+1}), and c_i→(a_{i−1},b_{i−1}). At level k use a_k→(a_{k−1},c_{k−1}), b_k→(b_{k−1},c_{k−1}), and c_k→(a_{k−1},b_{k−1}); the first edge is even. These are exactly the positive levelsets because every edge decreases distance by at most one and each vertex has a forward edge. Direct substitution gives h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1−i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. Thus Σ|g|=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). By harmonic duality, two switching flows with common supply φ≡1 have sink-1 inflows differing by exactly this amount. For k=2 an explicit certificate, listing (even,odd), is x: a1 (4/3,4/3), b1 (2,1), c1 (4/3,4/3), a2 (7/6,7/6), b2 (3/2,1/2), c2 (1/2,1/2); and y: a1 (7/3,4/3), b1 (1,1), c1 (11/6,5/6), a2 (5/3,2/3), b2 (1,1), c2 (1,0). Every nonsink has net outflow 1, while the sink-1 inflows are 10/3 and 11/6, differing by 3/2>1. For any fixed r>3, add r−3 vertices per level with successors (a_{i−1},b_{i−1}); the obstruction remains and the gap mass becomes k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)].

results.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
results.proof_sketch: Take L_1={a,b,c}, L_2={X,Y,Z}, with common edges a→(0,X), b→(0,Y), c→(0,1), and Z→(a,c). In completion A let X→(c,b) and Y→(a,b). Harmonicity gives h(c)=1/2, h(a)=h(X)/2, h(b)=h(Y)/2, hence h(a)=3/22>1/22=h(b). In completion B instead let X→(a,b) and Y→(c,a). The same equations now give h(a)=1/22<3/22=h(b). Both graphs are simple, have exactly three vertices in each positive level, and agree on the sinks and every outgoing edge from L_1. Thus the width-two procedure that orders a new level using only the preceding order and the current vertices' outgoing edges has no width-three analogue of that local form.

final_writeup:
Here “width r” necessarily means each positive level L_i, i≥1, since L_0 consists of the two sinks.

The target remains unresolved, but the analysis isolates both a positive finite-dimensional reduction and two rigorous obstructions to extending the supplied ladder proof. For any suffix with a fixed r-vertex absorbing boundary and fixed injection vector, harmonic duality places all integral boundary-inflow vectors in a box containing only O(N^(r−1)) integer points. Thus fixed width does prevent exponentially many boundary totals for one fixed supply.

However, the crucial ladder estimate is genuinely special to width two. The explicit three-rail family above has zero-player gap mass k(k+7)/(4(k+1)), and harmonic duality shows this is not merely slack in the proof: it is exactly realized as the difference between sink inflows of two switching flows with the same integer supply. The difference is already 3/2 for six nonsinks and grows linearly. Padding gives the same obstruction for every fixed r≥3.

The other structural ingredient also fails: two width-three completions with identical data through L_1 reverse the order of h(a) and h(b). Consequently, neither the constant switching-flow stability bound nor the local level-ordering recursion from the width-two proof extends to r=3. This only rules out those local proof ingredients; it does not rule out a different polynomial-time algorithm.

The boundary-signature bound does not by itself yield a polynomial algorithm. Backward edges from processed lower levels can produce different supply vectors at many future vertices, and the argument above only bounds signatures when that entire supply vector is fixed. Controlling or compressing those varying injections is therefore a precisely identified remaining obstacle.

Accordingly, this is valid partial progress only. No polynomial-time algorithm or contrary complexity classification has been proved for r=3, let alone for every fixed r>2, so the claimed resolution is PARTIAL rather than FULL.
